_doc: EXTRA set (release PRD S15): prompts added after baseline_1. Kept out of prompts.json so the 12-prompt score stays comparable across runs.
'seed': a script (relative to this file) run into the fresh document before the agent's model.py - the user's existing part. Fitness checks include seed objects.
Expectation keys as in prompts.json. Fitness keys: 'on_desk' (also implied by 'on a desk' in the prompt), 'allow_overlap' [[labelA, labelB], ...], 'gear_teeth', 'atech_check'.

ATECH prompts (S35) carry 'atech_check' and are reported as their own group (plain vs Atech pass rates). Atech fitness keys, measured on the document by fc_build.py: 'atech_modules' [names] each seated; 'board_upright' board plane within 30 deg of vertical (normal = least-variance axis of the board mesh); 'modules_inside' [names] each module's mesh box inside the box of the agent's Part shapes (0.5 mm tolerance; a necessary condition, not proof of enclosure).

doorbell_remote is the dogfood prompt (D45/S34) verbatim. Its 'min_objects': 2 is 'a snap-fit case is at least two parts'; the snap feature itself is not machine-checked. Buttons and screens may show through the case, so only the speaker is required inside. alarm_clock's board_upright follows from 'a screen facing the front' of a case on a desk: modules seat in the board plane (docs/ATECH_ASSEMBLY.md), so a front-facing screen needs a vertical board.

R173 (dogfood shift 4, prompts verbatim from the dogfood driver except where noted): 'overall_z' [lo,hi] = Z length of the tight world box of ALL the agent's parts (the product as it stands, whatever intent.json splits - D65). 'channels_open' {count, d}: round channels of that diameter (concave cylinders summing >= 180 deg about one axis), each open along its whole length: at 9 sections across the axis the channel centre lies in no closed loop (a C, not an O - D67). 'open_from_above' {min_depth_frac}: a vertical ray down the XY centre of every large object travels >= that share of the product height before meeting a part (a capped pot fails - D66). Atech fitness: 'open_along' [{module, toward: socket|face, min_open_pct}] = share of rays leaving the product without meeting an agent part, from the USB-C receptacle's mouth along its axis (the receptacle found in the module MESH by its 10.0 x 3.5 mm shell - D64) or from the module's face along the board normal; 'closed_around_board' = rays from the board centre along +-its three principal axes all meet an agent part. All measured with OCCT sections in fc_build.py, never with production's ray caster or intent.json (P2).

'edit' {prompt, expect} (R173, lead guidance 07:20 / D57): after the first request builds, run_eval sends this as a SECOND user turn on the same session (the fix loop runs again for it); the final score is against the edit's expect, the first request's own result is kept in `first_request`. enclosure_80x50x30's prompt adds 'Show it with the lid on.' to the dogfood text so 'overall Z' has one meaning.

Round 9 (R191/R192 regressions, dogfood shift 6 prompts verbatim: S6-3 c3mB, S6-2 c2n): 'volume_mm3' [lo,hi] = summed volume of the agent's parts (the toothbrush holder is 80*30*20 - 4*14*15*20 = 31200 exactly; +-1 %). 'notches_open' {count, w, min_depth, through, exact} = rectangular notches cut into a face (D74): gaps of width w between walls on a line across the part 0.5 mm inside the open face, each >= min_depth deep from that face and (through) open along the third axis; the best orientation counts; exact = the count must match. 'no_failed_verdict' = production's build.failures() on the final build is empty (Studio's red 'build still fails' never shows). 'insertion_path' {section_mm [W, t], min_depth_mm, min_mouth_mm} = the held object (a W x t phone section, its length along the way in) can reach its seat (D73): from each axis face, a grid of lines along the entry axis gives the free depth per column; the mouth is the widest run across t that stays free to min_depth_mm over a stretch of W; pass when the best mouth >= min_mouth_mm minus one grid step (0.5 mm). All measured with OCCT sections in fc_build.py (P2).

Round 10 (R202 / D77, dogfood S6-5 c5n prompt verbatim): 'hinge_opens' {bore_d [lo,hi], range_deg [a,b]} = the lid can swing open: the pin axis is MEASURED on the parts (a concave bore of bore_d on one axis line in two or more parts - the knuckles), the parts on it other than the largest are rotated about it from a to b in 5 deg steps in the sense that carries them away from the largest, and the check fails at the first angle where they share more than 0.01 mm3 with a part that does not move (the S6-5 lid: axis 3 mm inside the back face, 10.2 mm3 at 5 deg). Measured with OCCT in fc_build.py (P2), never ./check's motion sweep or intent.json.

Round 11 (R213 / D79 and R212 / D78, dogfood S7 prompts verbatim: c2n3 pegboard hook, c1n4 desk clock): 'mates' {board, thick_mm, hole_d, pitch, peg_d [lo,hi], min_pegs} = the reference object the prompt fully specifies is MODELLED where the part installs and the part's common with it, outside the holes the pegs pass through, is <= 0.01 mm3 (the c2n3 hook: 8 x 8 arm root 4.9 mm into a 5 mm 1/4-inch board). Placement is measured on the parts: pegs are convex cylinders of peg_d standing out of a flat face at least 2x their section; the board's front face is that face (the root farthest along the pegs when they disagree), its holes on the pitch grid through the pegs. min_pegs is 1: the board needs one peg to be placed, and a swept curl may have no cylinder. 'parts_engage' {min_parts, slide_mm} = every part but the largest that lies within slide_mm of another is slid slide_mm in 26 directions; when its blocked directions all fit in one open hemisphere it is held from one side only (a face touch, no lip, plug or hook in the opening - the c1n4 / c2n4 flat 2 mm end caps) and fails. min_parts 0 on the desk clock: the defect is a part that only touches, not the part count. Known limit: a lid held only by screws whose holes line up is a face touch here too. Both measured with OCCT in fc_build.py (P2), never ./check or intent.json.

prompts.prompt: Design a desk stand for the existing Clock_Enclosure in this document. It should hold the clock leaning back 15 degrees and stand on a desk. Show the clock seated in the stand.
Smart desk clock on the Atech 14-port board with a screen, a button and a speaker module, in a case that sits on a desk.
doorbell remote on the Atech board: put a button module and a speaker module on the board, then design a snap-fit case around the board with an opening over the button.
Weather station on the Atech 14-port board with a temperature and humidity sensor and a screen. The board stands upright in a case that sits on a desk.
Alarm clock on the Atech 14-port board: a screen facing the front, a snooze button and a speaker, in a case that sits on a desk.
Make me a small electronics enclosure, 80 x 50 x 30 mm outside, 2 mm walls, with a separate lid that sits on a 2 mm lip, and four M3 screw bosses in the corners. Show it with the lid on.

edit.prompt: Make the enclosure 10 mm taller, 40 mm outside overall with the lid on; keep everything else the same.

prompts.prompt: Put a light module and a USB-C power module on the Atech board, and design a fully closed box around it: no open ends, a removable lid held by two M3 screws, a window over the light and an opening for the USB-C plug.
A desk-edge cable clip: 40 mm long, it clamps onto a 25 mm thick desk top, and has three round 6 mm cable channels along its top, each with a 4.5 mm wide entry slot so the cable pushes in.
A self-watering planter: a 110 mm diameter outer reservoir 90 mm tall, an inner pot that sits in it with 6 drainage slots and a wick hole, and a fill spout on the side.
A toothbrush holder: a solid block 80 x 30 x 20 mm with four 14 mm wide slots cut 15 mm deep from the front edge, so the handles drop in from the top and the heads rest on the top face.

A phone tripod mount: a U-shaped cradle that holds a phone 9 mm thick and 75 mm wide, 30 mm deep, with 2 mm lips over the front edges, and on the bottom a 6.5 mm through hole for a 1/4-inch tripod screw with a hex pocket for a 1/4-20 nut (11.1 mm across flats, 5.5 mm deep).

A small box with a hinged lid: box 60 x 40 x 25 mm outside with 2 mm walls, and a separate 2 mm lid joined to it by a pin hinge along the back edge - three knuckles, alternating between box and lid, with a 2 mm hole through all of them for a 1.75 mm filament pin, and 0.3 mm clearance between the knuckles.

A pegboard hook for standard 1/4-inch pegboard (6.35 mm holes on 25.4 mm centres, 5 mm thick board): two pegs that go through two vertically adjacent holes, the top one curling down behind the board, and a 60 mm straight arm sticking out from the front, angled 15 degrees up.

Build a desk clock on the Atech board: a screen module, a speaker module for the alarm and a button module to snooze, in a stand-up case that leans the screen back about 15 degrees, with openings over the screen and the button and a grille over the speaker.
